definition: Software infrastructure used to systematically run a model against a suite of benchmarks or test cases and collect standardized performance metrics.
details: Evaluation harnesses (such as EleutherAI's lm-evaluation-harness) provide reproducible, standardized ways to compare models across many benchmarks, reducing inconsistencies that can arise from ad hoc, custom evaluation scripts.

explainer.lead: A harness is the software layer that runs a model against many benchmarks and records standardized scores, so comparisons mean something. Without it, results from different labs are hard to compare or reproduce.

tiers.eli5: It is like a standardized exam sheet and grading machine: every student gets the same questions and the same marking rules, so scores can be compared fairly.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers plug a model endpoint or weights into the harness and let it run the full benchmark suite with fixed prompts and scoring code. A common pitfall is harness and model version mismatches, where prompt formatting or tokenization differs from what the model saw in training and scores drop for the wrong reason.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, a harness is a pipeline mapping (model, task suite, prompt templates, scoring functions) to a metrics table; results are only comparable when all of these are held fixed. Known limits: fixed prompts may not reflect real usage, and public benchmarks can leak into training data.

explainer.example: Running lm-evaluation-harness over a new checkpoint on a dozen tasks yields one table of accuracy scores per task, comparable to previous checkpoints run under the same configuration.
